articles.title: DEEP SKY OBSERVING
articles.summary: This article presents a deep sky observing list compiled by Mark Wagner for July 2008, spanning the period from the third quarter to new moon. It details various celestial objects, including planetary nebulae, globular clusters, and open clusters, with challenge ratings, observational notes, and celestial coordinates. The list aims to guide observers from north to south, focusing on objects within one hour of right ascension.

articles.title: Phoenix from fire into ice
articles.summary: The article announces the successful landing of NASA's Phoenix Mars lander in the Martian north polar region, where it has begun analyzing soil samples for water, with its mission expected to last three months. It also details several celestial events for observers on Earth in July, including Jupiter at opposition, a close pass of Mars and Saturn, Venus entering the evening sky, and the visibility of Mercury, Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto.

articles.title: Solar Eclipses: Future Events and Travel Tips
articles.summary: This article explains solar eclipses, including the astronomical mechanics behind them, such as 'eclipse months' and the difference between total, annular, and partial eclipses. It highlights upcoming solar eclipses for 2008, 2009, 2010, and the next US-visible event in 2017, along with travel advice for those interested in observing these celestial phenomena. The author also provides recommendations for eclipse travel companies and mentions specific observing locations.

articles.title: Ozone, the Greenhouse Gas
articles.summary: Ozone, while known for blocking harmful UV light in the stratosphere and being a pollutant at the surface, also acts as a potent greenhouse gas at middle altitudes, trapping significantly more heat per pound than CO2. NASA's Aura satellite, equipped with the Tropospheric Emission Spectrometer (TES), provides unprecedented global data on this mid-altitude ozone, revealing its impact on climate change and the potential for increased concentrations due to industrialization.

articles.title: The SJAA Telescope Loaner Program: Overview, Selection, and Support
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers a telescope loaner program for members, providing various telescope types like Dobs and Schmitt Cassegrains for a three-month period, along with guidance for beginners and support through workshops. The article also features an announcement for the Exploratorium and NASA's live webcast and viewing party for the Total Solar Eclipse of 2008 from China, and new Spitzer telescope findings revealing Cassiopeia A as a Type IIb supernova.

articles.title: The Last 31 Days In Astronomy
articles.summary: This article, "The Last 31 Days In Astronomy," compiles significant astronomical news from May and June 2008. Key developments include the controversial reclassification of Pluto as a "plutoid," the successful launch of the GLAST gamma-ray telescope, and the Phoenix lander's arrival on Mars. Additionally, new research revealed the universe is twice as bright as previously thought, and a detailed Spitzer mosaic indicated the Milky Way possesses only two major spiral arms.
